title: Beyond the 956: Glen Hansard, Oscar-winning singer of “Falling Slowly” and star of “Once,” dies at 56
excerpt: Glen Hansard, the Irish singer-songwriter who won an Oscar for “Falling Slowly” and starred in the film “Once,” died July 29, 2026, in a motorcycle accident in Dublin. He was 56.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Glen Hansard, the Irish singer-songwriter who won an Academy Award for “Falling Slowly” and starred in the beloved film Once, died July 29, 2026, in a motorcycle accident in Dublin. He was 56.

Hansard was involved in a single-vehicle motorcycle accident in the early hours of July 29 in the Lucan area of Dublin, Irish police confirmed. He received treatment at the scene and was pronounced dead. His management, ATC Management, announced his death in a statement that morning. The Associated Press, Entertainment Weekly and The Times reported his death.

Born April 21, 1970, in Ballymun, Dublin, Hansard left school young and began his career busking on Dublin's Grafton Street. He founded the rock band The Frames in 1990 and later formed the folk duo The Swell Season with Markéta Irglová.

His widest audience came with Once in 2007, the low-budget musical film in which he starred as a street musician opposite Irglová. The film's song “Falling Slowly,” which they co-wrote, won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 2008.

Hansard was also known for co-founding Dublin's annual Christmas Eve busk on Grafton Street, a charity tradition for the Simon Community that began in 2010. His funeral was held August 4 at St. Patrick's Cathedral in Dublin, where U2's Bono read a tribute.

Rest in Peace, Glen Hansard.

Sources: The Associated Press; Entertainment Weekly; The Times; ATC Management.
